nodes.summary: The automorphism group of the full shift on $N$ symbols is the subgroup of the group of homeomorphisms of $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ onto itself consisting of the homeomorphisms $\varphi$ that commute with the unit shift $\sigma$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, that is, $\varphi \circ \sigma = \sigma \circ \varphi$.
nodes.title: Automorphism group of the full shift

nodes.summary: For $N \in \mathbb{N}$, the configuration space of the two-sided full shift on $N$ symbols is the set $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ of all bi-infinite sequences $x = (x_i)_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ of symbols. It carries the product of the discrete topologies.
nodes.title: Full shift space

nodes.summary: A map $f$ from the full shift $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $N$ symbols to itself is a one-dimensional cellular automaton if $f$ is continuous and commutes with the unit shift $\sigma$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, that is, $f \circ \sigma = \sigma \circ f$.
nodes.title: One-dimensional cellular automaton

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a map $f$ from the full shift $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $N$ symbols to itself, $P(f, k)$ is the number of configurations $x$ with $\sigma^k(x) = x$, where $\sigma$ is the unit shift given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, that are also periodic for $f$, that is, $f^n(x) = x$ for some $n \ge 1$. Here $k$ need not be the least period of $x$ under $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Joint periodic count

nodes.summary: For a map $f$ from the full shift $S_N$ on $N$ symbols to itself, the joint periodic growth rate is the real number
nodes.title: Joint periodic growth rate

nodes.summary: For a map $f$ from the full shift $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ on $N$ symbols to itself, the jointly periodic points of $f$ are the configurations $x$ that are periodic for $f$ and periodic for the unit shift $\sigma$, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$: there are $m \ge 1$ and $n \ge 1$ with $f^m(x) = x$ and $\sigma^n(x) = x$.
nodes.title: Jointly periodic points

nodes.summary: The unit shift $\sigma$ of the full shift on $N$ symbols, given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$, is a homeomorphism of $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ onto itself, with inverse given by $(\sigma^{-1} x)_i = x_{i-1}$.
nodes.title: The unit shift as a homeomorphism

nodes.summary: The unit shift on the full shift on $N$ symbols is the map $\sigma$ from $\{0, \dots, N-1\}^{\mathbb{Z}}$ to itself given by $(\sigma x)_i = x_{i+1}$ for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, the left translation by one step.
nodes.title: Unit shift

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
